title: Deep reconstructed coronary MRI is compared with CT angiography
summary: Adaptive-CS-Net reconstruction enabled noncontrast coronary MR angiography in a paired 64-patient study using CT angiography as the reference. Patient-level sensitivity and specificity for significant coronary narrowing were 92.0% and 84.6%, respectively. These diagnostic measurements came from a selected single-centre cohort; they do not establish replacement of CT angiography or improved patient outcomes.
organization: West China Hospital of Sichuan University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant Methods/results/limitations and exact front/canonical identity; current primary PubMed linked correction/retraction metadata checked.

evidence.tested: New paired coronary MRI and CT examinations, independently interpreted with CT angiography as the stenosis reference.
evidence.unknown: Larger external diagnostic studies and clinical outcome benefit remain unestablished; prospective acquisition alone does not prove prospective frozen-model outcome prediction.
evidence.ai_role: Adaptive-CS-Net combines learned CNN image representations with compressed-sensing reconstruction to make accelerated coronary MRI interpretable for stenosis assessment.
